title: Developer sandboxes | Slack Developer Docs
snippet:
A developer sandbox is an Enterprise org environment (a network of two or more Slack workspace instances) that can be used to build against all Slack features safely and securely, without an additional cost. The ability to provision sandboxes is a benefit offered by the [Slack Developer Program](https://api.slack.com/developer-program).
Every developer enrolled in the Slack Developer Program is eligible to provision a basic sandbox. Developers who are on a paid plan or who provide a valid payment method are able to access additional features.

All developers can provision a basic sandbox. If you are a member of a paid plan (the paid plan workspace must have been created at least 30 days ago, unless you're in an Enterprise organization) your sandboxes will have access to additional features. If you are not a member of a paid plan, you can also provide a payment method to access the full set of features, but note that you will not be charged.

If you are part of the [partner program](https://slack.com/partners), you will have the option of choosing from additional [templates](/tools/sandbox-template-demos).

- **Other limits**:
- Discovery API enablement is not available on sandboxes unless you are part of our [partner program](https://slack.com/partners).

As part of the [Slack Developer Program](https://api.slack.com/developer-program), you'll get access to an Enterprise organization sandbox that allows you to explore all features, including automations. You'll also get early access to betas, and can develop and test apps and workflows in a dedicated, fully-featured development environment.

Anyone can sign up for an account, and there are no costs associated with being a member of the Slack Developer Program. [Sign up](https://api.slack.com/developer-program/join) today!
Any developer enrolled in the Slack Developer Program can provision a basic developer sandbox. Any developer who is either on a paid plan or provides a valid payment method for the account can also access additional features in the sandbox.
If you find the basic sandbox is missing something you need to test with, you can unlock more advanced sandbox functionality by joining a paid plan workspace or adding a payment method. Adding a payment method won't charge you, it just confirms you're a human.

title: Slack developer FAQ | Slack Developer Docs
snippet:
You can provision sandbox environments by joining the [Slack Developer Program](https://api.slack.com/developer-program). Once you're ready to deploy your app, distributing the app will allow you to install it in other workspaces.

Are you a partner with us? The [Slack Partner Developer Program](https://api.slack.com/developer-program/partners) offers [partner sandboxes](https://api.slack.com/tools/partner-sandboxes).

When working with Slack apps or the [Web API](https://api.slack.com/apis/web-api/), you'll often need to send access tokens, also known as bearer tokens, along with inbound requests within the authorization header. When creating an app for the first time, you'll be given your own user and bot token while going through the app creation process. In order to obtain other users' tokens, you'll need to send users through the [OAuth 2.0 authentication flow](https://api.slack.com/authentication). When you're working with Slack apps, you'll be awarded access tokens after a user approves your application.
